name: Change request form
purpose: Describe a requested change, its impact on scope, time and cost, and capture written approval before work starts.
sections: CR details (ID, date, requested by, project)
example: Laravel booking platform for a UK clinic group
Add SMS appointment reminders 24 hours before each booking, with a link to cancel or reschedule.
Reduce no-shows, which the client estimates at 15% of bookings.
Change request: reminders were out of scope in the signed SOW (section 4.2).
New scheduled job, SMS template management in admin, cancel/reschedule deep link.
Development 5 days, QA 2 days, PM 0.5 day.
Milestone 3 moves by one week, from 28 March to 4 April.
Fixed price per the agreed rate card, invoiced with milestone 3.
Client provides a Twilio account and registered sender ID by 20 March.
Approved by client sponsor by signed form on 16 March; Oyelabs PM and account manager countersigned.

name: Minutes of meeting
purpose: Record attendees, decisions, action items and open points from a meeting, sent soon after it.
example: Client: product owner, marketing lead. Oyelabs: PM, tech lead, QA.
Demoed workout tracking and the subscription paywall. Client liked the flow; asked about Apple Health sync.
Apple Health sync is out of scope; PM to raise a CR for estimation.
Client to send final paywall pricing tiers – marketing lead – 14 April.
PM to send CR-004 for Apple Health sync – PM – 15 April.
Should free-trial length differ by country?

name: Status report (RAG)
purpose: Weekly one-page report of progress, RAG status, risks, issues and decisions needed, shared with the client and internal stakeholders.
example: Amber – Apple organisation enrolment still pending; go-live at risk by about one week.
Branding applied to all apps; two cities configured; custom loyalty module 70% done.
Loyalty module QA; TestFlight build to client.
D-U-N-S details mismatch may delay Apple enrolment (owner: client SPOC).
Confirm delivery fee per zone by 13 May.

name: Kickoff agenda
purpose: Agenda and checklist for the client kickoff meeting so goals, scope, governance and dependencies are agreed on day one.
example: Laravel + React marketplace for an Australian retailer
Launch a multi-vendor marketplace with 50 vendors within six months.
Discovery sign-off week 3; design approval week 6; UAT week 18; go-live week 20.
Weekly status report on Fridays; sprint demo every second Thursday; shared Slack channel.
Payment gateway account by week 4; product catalogue CSV by week 8.
Discovery workshops booked for next Tuesday and Thursday.

name: Requirement sign-off
purpose: Formal client confirmation that the documented requirements are complete and correct, freezing the scope baseline.
example: PRD v1.3 and 64 user stories in the project tracker
Laravel school-management system for a client in Kenya
Admissions, attendance, fees, exams and parent app.
Client provides existing student data in the agreed CSV format by week 5.
Changes after this sign-off go through the change request process.
Client sponsor (principal) on 2 June; Oyelabs PM on 2 June.

name: UAT sign-off
purpose: Formal client acceptance that the product passed user acceptance testing and may go live, listing any accepted known issues.
example: 112 scenarios tested; 109 passed; 3 minor issues logged.
Report export takes longer than 10 seconds above 5,000 rows; fix planned in v1.0.1.
Arabic translation review, moved to v1.1 by agreement.
The client accepts the release as meeting the agreed acceptance criteria for go-live.

name: Go-live checklist
purpose: Step-by-step checklist for go/no-go, cutover, store release, smoke test and rollback, with owners and status.
example: Production hosting, domain and store accounts in the client's name – Tech lead – done
Production keys (payments, SMS, maps) set and tested – Developer – done
Database backup taken before deployment – Tech lead – done
Go decision recorded in MoM with client sponsor – PM – done
Production deployment and migrations – Developer – done
Sign-up, booking, payment and notification flows – QA – done
iOS and Android released to the public – Developer – done
Rollback plan tested on staging; trigger: payment failure rate above agreed threshold – Tech lead – ready
Go-live email sent to client stakeholders – PM – done

name: Hypercare log
purpose: Log of every issue reported during hypercare and warranty, with classification, severity, owner and resolution times.
example: Drivers in one zone receive no new-order notifications.
Responded in 30 minutes; resolved in 4 hours (hotfix approved by tech lead and PM).
Zone ID missing from the notification topic after a configuration change; RCA shared.

name: Handover & KT checklist
purpose: Checklist of code, documentation, credentials, accounts and knowledge-transfer sessions needed for the client to own the product.
example: Repositories transferred to the client's GitHub organisation; final tag v1.2.0.
Architecture overview, local setup guide, API reference and admin manual in the shared drive.
All production credentials moved to the client's password manager; Oyelabs keys rotated.
AWS account owned by the client; Oyelabs IAM users to be removed after support ends.
Stripe, Twilio and Google Maps accounts in the client's name.
Three recorded sessions with the client's in-house developers: architecture, deployments, admin.
Two minor UI issues listed in the known-issues register.
Signed by client CTO on 30 September.

name: White-label onboarding checklist
purpose: Tracks everything a white-label client must provide or set up, from brand kit to accounts and listing content, with owners and dates.
example: Logo as SVG or 1024×1024 PNG with transparency – client – received
Primary and secondary colours (hex) and font – client – received
Apple Developer organisation account, Oyelabs invited as Admin – client – pending D-U-N-S
Google Play Console, Oyelabs invited with release permissions – client – done
Hosting account and domain in the client's name – client – done
Payment gateway live keys shared via password manager – client – pending
SMS provider with registered sender ID – client – in progress
Privacy policy and terms published on the client's domain – client – pending
Store descriptions in English and Arabic – client – draft received
Cities, delivery zones, commission and tax settings confirmed – client SPOC – done

name: RAID log
purpose: One register of risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies with owners, ratings, actions and status.
example: Risk – Apple organisation enrolment may take weeks because the client has no D-U-N-S number. Owner: client SPOC. Likelihood high, impact high. Action: start enrolment in week 1; open.
Assumption – Client supplies the product catalogue CSV in the agreed format by week 8. Owner: client SPOC. Validated at kickoff.
Issue – Payment gateway sandbox down for two days; checkout testing blocked. Owner: client SPOC. Action: escalated to client sponsor; open.
Dependency – Logistics partner API documentation from the client's courier. Owner: PM. Due week 6; received.

name: Escalation matrix
purpose: Who to contact at each escalation level, on both sides, for which kinds of problem and after how long.
sections: Time at previous level before escalating
example: Day-to-day delivery questions, blockers, delays under a week – PM and client SPOC.
Unresolved after the agreed window, a red RAG, or a P1 issue – delivery head and client operations lead.
Commercial disputes or unresolved level 2 matters – Oyelabs leadership and client founder.
Typical values agreed at kickoff and written into this sheet; illustrative only.
Email with the project ID in the subject, followed by a call for level 2 and 3.

name: Closure report
purpose: Summary at project end of what was delivered, how the project performed against plan, open items, lessons learned and next steps.
example: React Native fitness app for a US client, nine months
Launched on both stores; 10,000 sign-ups in the first month.
All 72 signed-off stories delivered; 5 CRs approved and delivered.
Go-live two weeks later than baseline, caused by CR-003 (approved date change).
Within the approved budget including CRs.
No P1 issues in hypercare; four minor known issues handed over.
Start store-account setup in week 1; consolidate design feedback through one SPOC.
Phase 2: Apple Health sync and coach dashboard.
Client sponsor and Oyelabs PM, 12 December.
